title: Polynomial-time initial-configuration test
statement: For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the binary alphabet and all natural numbers $d,c,A,a$, the function sending a bit string $y$ to the one-bit string containing the value of the following Boolean test is polynomial-time computable: take the first pair projection $x$ of $y$, form the encoding pairing $x$ with a pair consisting of the length-$vwid(A,a,|x|)$ prefix of the second projection of $y$ starting at offset $vwid(A,a,|x|)$ and the binary expansion of $vrad(d,c,|x|)$, and test whether that encoding belongs to the initial-configuration language for $N$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
caveat: The auxiliary functions $vwid$, $vrad$, and $cpAt$, and the initial-configuration language, have no supplied informal descriptions.
